newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: AMP NZ undecided on ideal pension solution.
newsitem.headline: AMP NZ undecided on ideal pension solution.

text.p: AMP New Zealand's Managing Director Rodney Cook said on Thursday the insurance and fund manager was undecided on what the ideal pension plan for the country would be as it faces a referendum on the issue.
But Cook told a news conference that New Zealand should not go down the same path as Australia, which had an award-based compulsory system that was complex and costly to administer.
However Cook said people may well decide on a small tax incentive to encourage pension savings.
Part of the new coalition government's policy is to abolish the pension surcharge and to hold a referendum on compulsory superannuation.
Cook said if anyone saved for 40 years at a real interest rate of 3.0 percent, the cost to them of a pension would be half that of "pay as you go".
"Against that, perhaps the community might think it is appropriate to provide some small tax incentive also such as tax rebates," Cook said.
Cook said the cost of New Zealand superannuation pension provision, as a proportion of GDP, is going down because of the change in the age of entitlement to 65 from 60.
But costs were set to rise sharply from 2001 as the first of the "baby boomers" reached retirement age.
AMP earlier announced plans to demutualise and list on the New Zealand and Australian Stock Exchanges in the second half of 1998. -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
